name: Fractal Industries Limited
summary: Fractal Industries is a garment manufacturer and marketplace fulfilment operator, not Fractal Analytics or an AI software company. The attractive interpretation is that retaining more of the apparel value chain can generate better margins and use IPO-funded inventory to scale. The decisive risk is that changing channels, large inventory commitments, tax-credit balances and platform dependence make accounting profit a poor guide to owner cash. FY26 group sales rose 5.08% to ₹89.7867 crore, while inventory rose 49.01% and two-year CFO/PAT was only 0.0272x. At the secondary 19 October close of ₹203, equity value is ₹159.3320 crore and reported current-share P/E 12.17x, but a defensible financed return is not established. This is a business-model transition watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder or eligible investment conclusion. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS because missing evidence is not converted into neutral scores. A comparable PPMP sell-through/unit-return bridge, current usable IPO cash, and complete tradability evidence would change the assessment. [S1–S4,S8–S10]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
GQS means Growth Quality Score. Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 4, EARN 5; investment factors R NS, D 4, P 5 and L NS. Each has material facts, an explicit contrary search and evidence IDs in the factor audit. The same factor value is reused without hidden size, order-book or TAM bonuses.

BQS known contribution = 0.20×5 + 0.20×4 + 0.10×5 + 0.10×3 + 0.08×5 + 0.08×4 = 3.32. Evidence coverage 76%; missing REV/CAP weight 24%; mathematical bound 3.56–5.72. GQS known contribution = 0.20×5 + 0.15×5 + 0.10×3 = 2.05. Coverage 45%; missing REV/CAP weight 55%; mathematical bound 2.60–7.55. Persistent cash weakness would cap a complete GQS at 5, yielding possible capped bounds 2.60–5.00, but the aggregate stays NS. IAS known contribution = 0.20×4 + 0.10×5 = 1.30. Coverage 30%; missing Q/R/L weight 70%; canonical mathematical bound 2.00–8.30. A tighter nested bound using BQS limits is 2.64–7.23; neither is an investment score. [E2–E11]

Score weights and factor products use exact Decimal arithmetic, with conventional half-up one-decimal display only after final computation. No missing weights are redistributed. Moving GOV and MOAT jointly by one point changes the known BQS contribution by 0.40, illustrating judgment uncertainty. No G1 or G3 evidenced-failure override is applied. G3 Hold alone does not exclude quality rankings; this record is unrankable because key quality factors are genuinely NS. No overall blended score or winner is supplied. [S1,S2]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Fractal participates in garment design, sourcing, in-house and outsourced manufacture, inventory storage and marketplace fulfilment. Products include shirts/tops/T-shirts, trousers and other bottomwear, ethnicwear and outerwear. Its customers and end buyers must be distinguished: a platform may be the commercial counterparty while many consumers supply end demand. FY25 sales were 92.47% B2C/PPMP and 7.53% outright B2B; Myntra accounted for 94.71% of marketplace-attributed sales, falling to 78.45% in the disclosed H1 FY26 mix. That is channel concentration even if individual consumers are numerous. [S2 pp. 259–260]

Under outright sale, Fractal sells garments at wholesale prices and the platform/customer owns stock after delivery. Under PPMP, Fractal forecasts demand, holds stock, sells through marketplace-owned brand rights, pays commissions and fulfilment charges, and bears returns/markdown and settlement risk. Cash is received after delivery, fees and return adjustments, not on factory dispatch. Revenue therefore captures a different part of the value chain than before; the higher selling-price/margin structure comes with more capital and operating risk. A customer/logo list is not evidence of pricing power. [S1 pp. 12–13; S2 pp. 84–86, 144 onward]

The owned 7ate9 brand is a new consumer experiment, not a proven branded franchise. Nested Brands generated only ₹0.1756 crore revenue and lost ₹0.4309 crore in FY26, with negative net worth ₹0.3309 crore. The parent owns 55%, so owner profit differs from consolidated group profit. The ₹10.0208 crore investment-property balance is not established surplus capital. The prospectus identifies Roop 2.1, 2.3 and 2.5 and Samhita 104 as warehouses, Roop 2.1A as operations office, and Tara as company guest house. These correspond to all six book balances. Their operating benefit can already support EBIT/EV; rental income of ₹0.0639 crore and an accounting classification do not prove separability. No separate property recovery is included in principal valuation cases. [S1 pp. 54, 130–139; S2 pp. 176–178]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Mechanism: integrated design-to-delivery processes may shorten lead times and reduce coordination costs. Evidence: established manufacturing, seven warehouses and direct platform integration. Durability depends on reliable availability, low return/fulfilment cost and platform retention. Failure mode: a platform can shift brand licences, change fees or allocate visibility to another vendor with equally reliable fulfilment. No quantified switching-cost, exclusivity duration, proprietary software revenue or price premium was located. This supports a useful operating capability, not a strong structural moat. [S1,S2]

Mechanism: owned consumer branding could capture more value and lessen dependence on third-party brands. Evidence is the actual 7ate9 launch and a subsidiary dedicated to marketing/trading. Contrary evidence is tiny revenue, losses, absent repeat-purchase/cohort contribution and unknown customer acquisition cost. Brand ambition is not brand equity. Inventory forecasts also create obsolescence risk before demand is proven. Neither the 23-year management-experience claim nor early profit growth establishes durable excess returns. [S1,S2]

Three relevant comparison lenses are Forcas Studio's FTX/value-apparel distribution, Kewal Kiran's established proprietary brands and integrated design-to-retail, and Gokaldas Exports' larger export-manufacturing/customer-qualification model. Forcas provides a closer apparel/channel comparison but not a borrowed quality score. KKCL illustrates brand ownership and diversified routes to market that Fractal has not yet demonstrated. Gokaldas illustrates manufacturing scale and global customer relationships, but export economics and trade risks differ from domestic PPMP. Reporting standards, lease treatment, working capital and brand spending differ. Matched 20 October peer valuations are ND, so no fabricated peer P/E average is used. Market share with a defensible denominator is also ND. [S15–S17]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The verified sequence is FY21 ₹10.2329005 crore, FY22 ₹92.8099405 crore, FY23 ₹88.9111 crore, FY24 ₹49.9440 crore, FY25 ₹85.4487 crore and FY26 ₹89.7867 crore. Annual additions are +₹82.5770400, −₹3.8988405, −₹38.9671, +₹35.5047 and +₹4.3380 crore. Five-year reported CAGR = (89.7867/10.2329005)^(1/5)−1 = 54.3983%; three-year reported CAGR = (89.7867/88.9111)^(1/3)−1 = 0.3272%. Ten-year CAGR is ND because the company was incorporated only in 2020. The original audited FY21 revenue, visually checked, is used instead of confusing an aggregator's ₹2.2668 crore FY24 PAT with an early revenue number. [S1–S4]

The small first-year base is not automatically a distorted base and receives no discretionary penalty. However, an explicit economic-comparability issue exists: outright wholesale revenue was 100% of FY23 and 94.66% of FY24, but only 7.53% in FY25. PPMP consumer receipts, marketplace fees, return economics and inventory ownership differ. FY24 sales to promoter-linked Fractal Fashion were ₹25.2553 crore, 50.57% of sales, versus ₹15.8772 crore in FY23; the later platform route eliminates that customer category but does not independently identify same-product end demand. Price, units, channel mix, old-stock clearance and third-party versus related sell-through have not been reconciled. Subsidiary revenue is immaterial in the recent total, but this alone does not solve gross economic comparability. [S2 pp. 259–271]

Reported FY26 growth is 5.08%, not 71%: the latter belongs to the FY25 rebound. H1 FY26 prospectus revenue was ₹47.2973 crore; the FY26 total implies balancing H2 ₹42.4894 crore, which must not be mislabeled a single quarter or mechanically annualized. Current FY27 H1 results were not located in the retrieved register through cutoff; inaccessible exchange attachments mean this is a search limitation, not proof that no filing exists. REV therefore remains NS until a consistent underlying-demand basis can be established; neither favorable nor unfavorable period is selected opportunistically. [S1,S2,S13,S14]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The accessible runway is digital apparel fulfilled through existing marketplace relationships, plus an early own-brand route. Management's prospectus used ₹100 crore FY26 sales and ₹130 crore FY27 sales for working-capital planning. Actual FY26 standalone sales of ₹89.6115 crore missed the former by 10.39%; achieving the latter now needs approximately 45.07% growth, not merely 30%. This is a management planning assumption, not a funded order book. No binding multi-year backlog or contracted consumer demand was established. [S1,S2]

The prospectus's capacity table reports 4.44 million installed units and 2.76 million utilized units at September 2025, 62.16%; FY25 figures were 2.376 million and 1.824 million, 76.77%. Capacity period/annualization, own manufacture versus job work and sold-stock realization are not fully reconciled. Website claims of 4.5 lakh monthly units are not silently substituted for the dated prospectus table. The model therefore calibrates revenue to an explicitly assumed ₹500 per equivalent sold unit, not a disclosed ASP. Base 10% annual sales growth, 14% EBIT margin and ONWC of 50% of sales require working capital and capex; bull 18% growth/18% margin/45% ONWC requires better turnover and sustained economics. Six annual rows expose utilization equivalents and funding, rather than merely multiplying sales. [S1,S2]

Including the properties in operating capital, the three-year incremental accounting proxy is 23.24%: normalized operating NOPAT rises ₹9.74876 crore against ₹41.9400 crore additional equity+NCI+debt−cash. A narrower proxy subtracting all property investments produces 26.21% against ₹37.1960 crore, but that exclusion is not supported by the disclosed operational uses. The operating bridge shows ₹37.1020 crore additional broad working capital, ₹0.0020 crore additional net PPE and ₹0.0920 crore other-net-asset residual. Cumulative FY24–26 cash capex ₹0.9292 crore less D&A ₹0.9205 crore differs slightly from net PPE change because of disposal/scope/rounding. Yet margin gains occurred during wholesale-to-PPMP migration and an unusually large logistics-cost reduction. That cannot be attributed to returns on new inventory cohorts. The added property balance is ₹4.7440 crore. Although disclosed property uses are operational, project/cohort attribution, stock ageing, sell-through contribution and a comparable five-year IC denominator remain missing. CAP stays NS; current ROIC is not its substitute. [S1–S4]

GQS is NS with 45% coverage. Persistent cash weakness creates a cap at 5 only if the aggregate becomes scoreable; it does not erase missing REV/CAP. Growth that requires increasingly slow inventory and uncertain tax-credit recovery is not proven high-quality compounding. [S1,S2]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Pankaj Bishwanath Agrawal is chairman/managing director; Priti Agrawal is a promoter. March 2026 promoter/group ownership was about 69.07%, with Pankaj alone 66.57%. Directors' FY26 remuneration of ₹0.6335 crore is about 4.91% of group PAT and 15.54% of CFO, not an automatically excessive amount. Historical related-party sales and receivables were material: Fractal Fashion receivable ₹11.0852 crore in FY23 and ₹3.1128 crore in FY24 disappeared in later restated balances. This is a concentration/collection history requiring reconciliation, not proof of fake sales. [S1,S2]

The September AGM notice proposed ₹10 crore FY27 transactions with 55%-owned, loss-making Nested Brands and up to ₹50 crore loans/guarantees/security involving interested entities under Section 185. ₹50 crore is about 67.78% of closing owners' equity. The discovery register says the resolutions passed; the primary voting attachments were inaccessible, so approval and actual deployment are not conflated. No ₹50 crore loan is assumed to have been advanced. A separate maximum-use stress quantifies the possible consequence. A subsidiary RPT permission is not third-party profit or free funding. [S1 pp. 22–37; S13,S14]

Capital raising: 7,297 shares were privately placed on 1 July 2025 at ₹1,530 each; the subsequent 10:1 bonus produced 5,072,970 additional shares and changed unit prices, not proportional ownership. The split-adjusted private price is about ₹139.09 versus the February IPO ₹216, with timing/risk differences acknowledged. The IPO issued 2,268,600 new shares for ₹49.00176 crore; no OFS. Current shares exceed pre-IPO 5,580,267 by 40.66%, so historical weighted EPS must not price the current capitalization. Net cash receipts after ₹5.1585 crore issue costs plus pre-IPO cash reconcile to ₹44.959701 crore; the cash-flow statement's capital/premium sublabels include bonus transfers, but the combined total is not an extra cash receipt. [S1,S2]

Promises versus delivery: FY26 ₹100 crore sales plan versus ₹89.6115 crore actual is a clear miss; own-brand commercialization planned for FY26 was reported launched, but subsidiary sales remain tiny and losses material relative to its own size; IPO working-capital use was partially deployed by March with substantial funds unspent. The FY27 target has no verified current result at cutoff. Auditor changes across early years are recorded, but no resignation citing missing information was found; FY26 opinions are unmodified. Tax contingency ₹0.7019 crore and late statutory payments warrant monitoring, not a fraud label. [S1–S4,S13]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Historical ₹ crore operating bridge, with scope labels and full inputs embedded below: FY23 revenue 88.9111, operating EBITDA 4.1312, EBIT 3.8173, group PAT 2.6578, CFO 8.0144, cash capex 0.8014 and FCF proxy 7.2130; FY24 49.9440, 3.9878, 3.6381, 2.2656, −10.0143, 0.1146 and −10.1289; FY25 latest comparative 85.4487, 11.0877, 10.7945, 7.5198, −3.5208, 0.4317 and −3.9525; FY26 89.7867, 17.2689, 16.9913, 12.9036, 4.0765, 0.3829 and 3.6936. EBITDA here excludes other income and uses after-prior-period PBT consistently. The report's headline EBITDA ₹17.5400 crore includes other income; FY25 headline also adds back prior-period expense. These are disclosed bridges, not interchangeable labels. Group PAT is used for CFO comparison; ₹13.0975 crore parent-attributable profit is used for equity EPS. [S1,S2]

FY25–26 ratio of sums is ₹0.5557 crore CFO/₹20.4234 crore PAT = 0.0272x, not the mean of annual ratios. FY24–26 mixed-perimeter ratio is −0.4169x; it is indicative, not a perfectly constant-scope series. FY21/FY22 statements classify short-term borrowing changes inside CFO; the embedded data retain raw values and remove those movements in separate diagnostics. No false six-year cash-conversion statistic is claimed. FY25 restated prospectus PAT ₹7.5376 crore differs from later comparative ₹7.5198 crore by ₹0.0178 crore; CFO differs by ₹0.0015 crore. These minor differences and older original/restated rows are retained rather than silently selected. [S1–S5]

FY26 CFO bridge begins PBT ₹15.7540 crore, adjusts depreciation, gratuity, interest and FD income, then absorbs ₹12.8607 crore inventory and ₹3.8231 crore loans/advances while receivables release ₹0.9588 crore and payables contribute ₹5.2718 crore. Cash tax is ₹2.7763 crore. Nearly all short-term advances are ₹9.9855 crore balances with revenue authorities, not ordinary customer lending; recovery/offset timing matters. Capex ₹0.3829 crore is investing cash flow and does not explain weak CFO. Reported CFO also precedes ₹1.5084 crore financing interest, so FY26 CFO less capex and interest is only ₹2.1852 crore. [S1 pp. 116–117, 134–139]

Average receivable days improve from 28.19 to 27.18, while material-COGS-proxy inventory days worsen from 213.95 to 263.09; this denominator excludes labor/logistics and is explicitly not full COGS. Payable days on purchases are 62.44; the corresponding partial-cost cash cycle is 227.83 days. Closing receivables include ₹0.2057 crore older than six months, but no disclosed doubtful balance. Inventory ageing/markdown provisions and tax-asset recovery schedules are missing. Raw materials, WIP and finished goods total ₹39.0997 crore, of which finished goods ₹31.6537 crore dominate fashion risk. [S1]

Reported cash ₹31.3313 crore includes ₹30.6608 crore FDs; cash/ordinary bank balances only ₹0.6705 crore. Debt ₹11.5171 crore includes CC ₹7.5061 crore, total property-bank term principal ₹2.7983 crore and director demand loans ₹1.2127 crore. Current term maturities ₹0.8809 crore are already inside that total. Net cash using all reported FDs is ₹19.8142 crore, but is not asserted freely available. IPO unutilized disclosure ₹32.8318 crore exceeds group cash by ₹1.5005 crore; encumbrances, cost accruals and permitted-use reconciliation are open. Interest cover is 11.26x. Average broad ROIC is 25.91% including property, versus 32.65% under the narrower all-property-excluded denominator; neither is CAP proof. [S1,S2]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹203 and 7,848,867 current shares, equity value is ₹159.3320 crore. FY26 owner EPS on current shares is ₹16.6871, giving P/E 12.17x; the reported weighted EPS ₹22.48 would understate the true current-share multiple. P/B is 2.16x. Enterprise value is ₹139.5178 crore if all reported cash is netted, or ₹170.1786 crore if only cash excluding FDs is netted. All-cash EV/operating EBITDA is 8.08x. Reported CFO-minus-capex yield is 2.32%, before financing interest. These cross-checks do not establish intrinsic value. [S1,S8,S10]

The primary return method is a linked annual operating/cash/funding model and terminal EBIT enterprise-value bridge. It models tax 26%, interest 9%, capex, depreciation, ONWC, contractual and demand debt repayment, full issued shares, NCI economic claims and zero separate property recovery in principal cases. No renewal is assumed: year-one principal payments ₹9.5997 crore include demand CC/director debt and current term maturity; remaining bank principal runs off subsequently. Opening IPO cash is counted once, no fresh IPO receipt is added, and no dividend is both paid and retained. Six fiscal rows FY27–FY32 support exact five-calendar-year investor returns via a 19 October 2031 interpolated terminal balance. Entry and exit costs are each an illustrative 2%, not an observed spread. [S1,S2]

Ordinary cases use only ₹0.6705 crore cash excluding all FDs. Bear/base/bull have respective peak cash-buffer gaps ₹7.6142/₹8.0946/₹2.7670 crore. Their ordinary terminal prices and returns are null, not an impossible negative-cash valuation. Separate conditional full-FD-release paths use ₹31.3313 crore once: bear growth −20%, then flat, then 3%, 8% EBIT and 7x terminal EBIT; base 10% growth, 14% EBIT, 50% ONWC and 10x; bull 18% growth, 18% EBIT, 45% ONWC and 13x. With zero separate property add-on, conditional terminal prices are ₹101.04/₹335.44/₹746.47 and cost-adjusted five-year returns −13.72%/9.69%/28.71%. These are assumption-dependent diagnostics, not funded targets or scoreable R. [Embedded annual models; S1,S2,S10]

The principal scenarios assign zero separate recovery to the ₹10.0208 crore property book. S2 pp. 176–178 identifies warehouses, operations office and company guest house, not assets established as surplus to modeled operations. Removing other income does not remove rent savings or operating benefits from EBIT. Separate unsupported asset-recovery sensitivities show what 50% base or 75% bull recovery would add: ₹341.83/₹756.05 prices and 10.10%/29.04% returns. These can double count operating benefits because replacement/leaseback costs and disposability are not established; they are not the principal cases or scoreable targets. [S1,S2]

Hypothetical debt rescue is isolated: base requires ₹8.0946 crore new uncommitted borrowing and gives 6.80% diagnostic return after its debt/interest claims. A separate roughly ₹10 crore equity rescue at ₹140, 5% issue costs and whole new shares gives about 6.02% with 8,563,153 shares; it is not an announced issue. Neither rescue supplies missing authorization or financing evidence. The model also tests collections +30 days, margin −3 points, logistics cost rebound, extra capex, receivable losses, higher interest and the separate maximum Section 185 deployment. [S1]

At base economics and full FD release, the 15% hurdle requires about 16.80% annual sales growth, versus 13.02% at a 12% hurdle and 20.45% at 18%. The conditional base entry prices for 12/15/18% hurdles are ₹182.87/₹160.23/₹140.87; these are not buy levels while funding/economics are unverified. A full 3×3 growth (5/10/15%) versus terminal multiple (7/10/13x) grid embeds all annual rows. There is no DCF terminal-growth illusion, no probabilistic average of IRRs, and no borrowed peer valuation premium. R and IAS remain NS. [S1,S2,S10]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-impairment risk is High, not because SME status implies wrongdoing, but because platform economics and stock funding can fail together. A credible path is weaker marketplace visibility or a brand-right/fee change → slower sell-through and more returns → lower gross contribution and higher logistics/marketing costs → ageing inventory and tax-credit cash absorption → demand-debt repayment or reduced drawing power → asset sale or discounted capital issue. Common shareholders bear losses after creditors, and dilution can permanently reduce their claim even if the company survives. [S1,S2]

The single decisive variable is cash contribution from sell-through after marketplace fees, logistics, returns and the capital tied in stock. Accounting margin alone is not enough. Strongest contrary evidence to the cautious thesis is the ₹31.3313 crore reported cash position, low closing debt and 11.26x interest cover. If the FDs are accessible for their authorized purposes, ordinary operations might be well funded. Accordingly G3 is Hold, not Fail, and insolvency is not alleged. Conversely an unverified cash label cannot be treated as an unrestricted balance. [S1]

Conditional full-FD bear price ₹101.04 represents 50.23% downside before comparing any rescue dilution; the cash-locked linked stress requires ₹18.0152 crore buffer. Full FD availability eliminates that annual cash gap but still produces about −16.26% five-year diagnostic return under linked stress. The separate ₹50 crore related-entity allocation stress generates a ₹27.4338 crore buffer need even with all reported cash; that is a risk-limit illustration, not evidence the amount has been advanced. Inventory book values and property costs are not liquidation floors, and no independent property appraisal or creditor-priority recovery estimate was obtained. Normal price volatility or one missed half-year is not itself thesis failure; recurring negative contribution, unusable cash or material unapproved leakage would be. [S1,S2]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome requires about 37.97% annual price growth over five years; tenfold requires 58.49%. Over ten years these become 17.46% and 25.89%. These are arithmetic requirements, not probabilities or expected returns. The identity separates revenue, common-owner margin, fully diluted shares and terminal multiple; a bonus issue does not itself create economic value. [S1,S2]

At unchanged shares, FY26 current-share EPS ₹16.6871 and a 12x terminal P/E, prices of ₹1,015 and ₹2,030 require owner earnings of roughly ₹66.39 crore and ₹132.78 crore, respectively. At an assumed 10% owner net margin, that implies about ₹663.9 crore and ₹1,327.8 crore sales, many times the current ₹89.79 crore base and beyond the disclosed 4.44 million-unit capacity at the model's merely illustrative ₹500 realization. These goals require substantial additional capacity or outsourcing, stock funding, platform diversification and much stronger cash conversion. Lower terminal multiples and equity dilution increase the burden. The embedded five-year bull diagnostic, despite 18% sales growth and sustained margins, is below 5x the starting price. Classification: speculative/unsupported as a five-year base thesis; a ten-year entrepreneurial possibility is not evidence-backed compounding. [S1,S2,S10]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. PPMP sell-through and contribution: baseline FY25 92.47% PPMP and 94.71% Myntra channel share. On each future result, obtain units sold, returns, gross invoices, fees and net realized contribution. A platform concentration decline is useful only if cash margins persist; recurring negative contribution is a thesis break. [S2]
2. Inventory and ageing: ₹39.0997 crore at March 2026, +49.01% against 5.08% sales growth. Investigate another period of stock growth materially above comparable sell-through, rising aged finished goods or clearance losses; do not treat a single seasonal build as automatic failure. [S1]
3. Cash conversion: FY25–26 CFO/PAT 0.0272x. Require a credible collection/stock/tax bridge and material cumulative improvement; positive PAT with another large operating cash deficit raises the funding hold. Include interest paid in the financing bridge. [S1]
4. IPO cash and FDs: reconcile ₹30.6608 crore FDs and ₹32.8318 crore unutilized proceeds to banks, maturity/lien status and permitted objects. Investigate the ₹1.5005 crore disclosed difference before assigning availability. Material unexplained or unauthorized use would change G1/G2, not just valuation. [S1]
5. Tax-authority balances: ₹9.9855 crore. Obtain ageing, expected refund/offset date and actual post-March realization. A prolonged increase without recovery enlarges working-capital need and weakens CAP evidence. [S1]
6. Funding terms: CC ₹7.5061 crore and director loans ₹1.2127 crore are demand obligations; bank current term maturity ₹0.8809 crore. Verify current drawing power, renewal, covenants and cash coverage before an investment conclusion. Historical ₹18 crore sanction is not enough. [S1]
7. Own-brand and RPT allocation: Nested revenue ₹0.1756 crore, loss ₹0.4309 crore; proposed trade ceiling ₹10 crore and broader interested-entity ceiling ₹50 crore. Track actual cash transfers, returns, approvals and recoverability. Authorization alone is not deployment. [S1,S13]
8. Sales-plan delivery and cost durability: FY26 parent revenue ₹89.6115 crore versus ₹100 crore plan; logistics expense declined ₹10.2737 crore. Require explanation and recurrence before extrapolating 14–18% scenario margins or the FY27 ₹130 crore plan. [S1,S2]
9. Tradability before implementation: retrieve complete official 20/60-session turnover, verified zero-trade days, lot, surveillance status, bid–ask and executable depth. Four/five lots are ₹4.872/₹6.09 lakh at the research quote, not guaranteed exit proceeds. Monitoring here is a research recommendation only; no automation or trade was created. [S8–S14]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold — unresolved evidence and funding/tradability; research-priority business-model transition watchlist. BQS NS (76% coverage; bounds 3.56–5.72), GQS NS (45%; raw bounds 2.60–7.55, possible cap 5), IAS NS (30%; bounds 2.00–8.30). The numerical classification matrix cannot assign a valid cell to missing aggregates. There is no evidence-backed compounder designation and no buy/sell instruction. G1 has no evidenced severe failure; G3 Hold is not a default or funding-failure verdict. [S1,S2]

The 12.17x reported P/E makes the name worth understanding rather than dismissing as obviously expensive, but low quoted multiple does not repair weak cash realization or the current funding information gap. Price alone could improve conditional returns but cannot create missing unit economics, confirm FDs or make a thin market executable. Complete evidence could eventually support either a selective value/transition thesis or a weaker business conclusion; the present record does not pre-judge that outcome with a fabricated neutral score. [S1,S10]

Reopen after a reconciled wholesale-to-PPMP volume/price/fee bridge, matured inventory/cohort returns, actual cash/tax-credit realization, bank-backed current liquidity and a complete tradeability sample. Recompute factors before ranking. G3 Hold alone would not bar numerical quality rankings; actual missing REV and CAP do. An existing holder would need position size, cost/tax context and live exit depth before any implementation discussion. No transaction or external communication has been made as part of this research. [S1,S2,S8–S14]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger supplies document dates, working primary URLs, printed-page/PDF locators, local hashes and access status. Historical filing facts are V; arithmetic is C; management planning/capacity statements are M; forecast, tax, cost-of-capital, fees, property recovery, NCI allocation and funding scenarios are A. Evidence IDs attach claims to sources, and the canonical JSON embeds complete historical inputs, annual scenarios, stresses, two-way sensitivities, reverse expectations and raw liquidity observations. Private file paths are not a substitute for model data. [S1–S18]

Most important limitations: (i) wholesale-to-PPMP economic comparability and pre-transition related-party sell-through; (ii) incremental stock-cohort profitability rather than current ROIC; (iii) current FD liens/maturities and IPO-use reconciliation; (iv) tax-credit recoverability, stock ageing and actual margin normalization; (v) current credit drawing power and post-March obligations; (vi) complete BSE trade series, bid–ask, restrictions and September ownership/pledges. The recent announcement register is discovery evidence only when primary attachments are inaccessible. Missing 22 liquidity dates are neither fabricated trades nor confirmed zeros. [S1,S2,S8–S14]

Reporting reconciliation: annual KPI page labels rupee-lakh amounts as millions and shows unadjusted EPS comparisons; audited statement units and note 29 are used instead. The text also has inconsistent brand spelling and copy-editing errors. These are disclosure-quality warnings, not proof of manipulated accounts. FY25 original/restated/latest comparative differences are retained. The capital/premium cash-flow sublabels are reconciled at their combined net cash level, so a noncash bonus is not counted as new funding. Negative NCI is not added to common equity value. Ordinary unfunded returns remain null and rescues stay separate. [S1–S7]

Analytical assumptions: 26% normalized tax; 12–16% nominal capital-cost comparison; 9% initial debt interest with stress; six fiscal projection rows and exact five-year investor horizon; ₹1 crore diagnostic liquidity buffer; 2% entry and exit friction; explicit scenario margins, capital and multiple paths; no payout or probability assignments. These are reproducible hypotheses, not management guidance or fair-value facts. The framework is a research convention, not a statistically validated return predictor. A full model/source QA report and reproducible backups accompany the record. [S1,S2]
